legend: At the Latin America ICPC Championship 2026, the problemsetter's team ran into a tricky problem. One of the members on the team, Avnith immediately recognized the problem and claimed that it is trivially solved by [REDACTED]. However, the problem was actually solved by Centroid Decomposition and NTT. During the flight back from Chile, the problemsetter could not forget about the incident and made a problem based on [REDACTED]. Now it is your job to figure out what [REDACTED] is and solve the problem.
You are given an undirected tree with n$$$n$$$ vertices and an integer k$$$k$$$.

For every vertex r$$$r$$$ considered as the root, define dr(v)$$$d_r(v)$$$ to be the distance from r$$$r$$$ to v$$$v$$$. For every k$$$k$$$-vertex subset S$$$S$$$, let lcar(S)$$$lca_r(S)$$$ be the lowest common ancestor of all vertices in S$$$S$$$ in the tree rooted at r$$$r$$$.

Let f(r)=∑S∈V|S|=kdr(lcar(S))
$$f(r)=\sum_{\substack{S\in V\\|S|=k}} d_r(lca_r(S))$$ In other words, the sum of the depths of the least common ancestor of all sets with k$$$k$$$ vertices if the tree is rooted at vertex r$$$r$$$.
Find f(r)$$$f(r)$$$ for each r$$$r$$$ from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$. Since the answers may be large, output them modulo 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$.
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$, k$$$k$$$ (1≤n,k≤2⋅105)$$$(1 \leq n,k \leq 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ as denoted in the problem statement.
The next n−1$$$n-1$$$ lines contain two integers each line, denoting an edge in the tree.
Tests in subtasks are numbered from 1−25$$$1−25$$$ with samples skipped. Each test is worth 10025=4$$$\frac{100}{25}=4$$$ points.
output: One line with n$$$n$$$ integers; the i$$$i$$$-th integer denotes f(i)$$$f(i)$$$ modulo 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$.
